search_log: Searched "Light from Heaven" "Jan Karon" excerpt and opened the Penguin Random House excerpt plus CBS's publisher-permission republication of the same Chapter One text.
Searched "Light from Heaven" "Jan Karon" "third person", narrator, and point of view; no credible source explicitly labeled the whole book's grammatical person.
Searched the title with epistolary, multiple narrators, and alternating narration; found no evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
Searched for Chapter Two, later chapter titles, and distinctive interior quotations; Google Books exposed bibliographic information and a table of contents but no usable sustained interior prose.
The CBS excerpt duplicated the publisher's opening rather than extending structural coverage, so it was not counted as independent evidence.

A retailer-aggregated user review mentioned point-of-view shifts but did not identify a change in grammatical person; it was treated as a focalization comment rather than contrary narrative-person evidence.
person_note: The authorized opening is sustained third-person narration centered mainly on Father Tim, and the later Goodreads passages q00175 and q00176 independently show the same external third-person narrating position. First-person forms elsewhere are prayers, dialogue, or universal maxims; q00166 is explicitly confirmed as Father Tim's speech. Targeted research found no epistolary, second-person, or alternating-person structure. The main limitation is that the authorized online prose is confined to Chapter One, but diagnostic interior quote evidence corroborates it.
